questions_and_answers.question_text: How are combined direction names ordered in Chinese?
Which three provinces make up Dōngběi?
Why is the Northeast called Manchuria?
What is notable about le after -guo?
Give the Chinese for northwest, northeast, southwest, and southeast.
What is the status of the Mǎn language today?

answers.answer_text: It is well on its way to extinction — most Mǎn speak only Chinese.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is Dàqìng, and why is it significant?

answers.answer_text: China's leading crude-oil producer; its development largely enabled China to meet her own oil needs by 1963.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What slogan did Máo Zédōng issue in 1964?

answers.answer_text: Gōngyè xué Dàqìng — "Learn from Dàqìng in industry."

questions_and_answers.question_text: Which dynasty was run by the Manchus?

articles.text:
7. A: Dōngběi, Xīběi nǐ dōu qùguo le You've been to Manchuria and the
      ba?                            Northwest, haven't you?
   B: Zài Dōngběi wǒ zhǐ cānguānle  In Manchuria I've only visited Dàqìng,
      Dàqìng, Xīběi hái méi qù ne.   and I haven't been to the Northwest yet.

Notes on No. 7

Dōngběi, Xīběi: COMBINED DIRECTION NAMES are said in the REVERSE ORDER from English:

xīběi (west-north)    = northwest      dōngběi (east-north)  = northeast
xīnán (west-south)    = southwest      dōngnán (east-south)  = southeast

Dōngběi: "the Northeast," "Manchuria." The northeastern region of China, consisting of the three provinces of Liáoníng, Jílín, and Hēilóngjiāng, is sometimes called Manchuria because the largest indigenous minority is the MANCHU, or Mǎn, nationality. Of China's 2.6 million Mǎn, most live scattered throughout these three provinces and Héběi.

The Mǎn, and before them their ancestors the Nǚzhēn (Nuchen, an ancient nationality of the same region), were a MAJOR FORCE in Chinese history — from the Jīn Dynasty, in which the Nǚzhēn ruled northern China for over a century (1127–1234), to the Manchu-run QĪNG Dynasty (1644–1911). After the Qīng dynasty established its capital in Běijīng, great numbers of Mǎn filtered south and intermixed with the Han Chinese.

In this century, large-scale Han migration to the Northeast has caused the region's population to swell to 99.4 million (1976 estimate), of which only 2.4 million are of the Mǎn nationality. Although their ethnic origins are distinct, the Mǎn today are virtually ASSIMILATED with the Han racially, culturally, and linguistically. Most speak only Chinese; the Mǎn LANGUAGE is WELL ON ITS WAY TO EXTINCTION.

Xīběi: "the Northwest," a region which includes Níngxià, Xīnjiāng, Qīnghǎi, Shǎnxī, and Gānsù.

qùguo le: "have gone to." Notice that NEW-SITUATION LE may FOLLOW a verb phrase with the ending -GUO.

A: Nǐ chīguo fàn le ma?          Have you eaten yet?
B: Chīguo le.                    Yes.

Dàqìng: An OIL-PRODUCING CENTER in southern Hēilóngjiāng province. Dàqìng is the nation's LEADING PRODUCER of crude oil, accounting for more than one third of the crude oil volume. China's oil industry has only developed since 1949, and it was the monumental exploration and drilling at Dàqìng, under extremely adverse conditions, that in large part enabled China to MEET HER OWN OIL NEEDS BY 1963. In 1964, Máo Zédōng called on the whole nation to LEARN FROM DÀQÌNG IN INDUSTRY (Gōngyè xué Dàqìng), a slogan which continued to be heard through the Cultural Revolution.
